svg.desc: Editable educational infographic created locally by JARVIS. Text and illustrations are vector elements.

g.text: Element discovery transformed chemistry: from identifying substances in minerals and gases to detecting atoms made in laboratories.
DISCOVERER: Carl Wilhelm Scheele · Uppsala, Sweden
Scheele produced greenish-yellow chlorine by heating
hydrochloric acid with pyrolusite. Humphry Davy later
Courtois saw violet vapour while processing seaweed ash.
Gay-Lussac later named the element after its violet
Balard identified an orange-red liquid in brine residues.
Carl Löwig had independently produced a sample in 1825.
Janssen and Lockyer independently detected a new yellow
line in the Sun’s spectrum. Helium was isolated on Earth

Calcium-48 ions were fused with berkelium-249. IUPAC

Discovery advanced from chemical isolation and solar spectroscopy to accelerator-made nuclei through international collaboration.
KEY TAKEAWAY: Evidence matters: first observation, isolation, synthesis and official recognition can occur in different years.
Sources: Royal Society of Chemistry element histories · ACS Transuranium Elements at Berkeley Lab · IUPAC discovery and naming reports.
